inputs.original_text: The owner of Blue Waters has said that Government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything”.Perhaps this might be considered as an environmental tax. Plastic bottles can be found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains, which then enter...
inputs.modified_text: The Blue Waters owner is right to challenge a government that takes taxes while rivers and drains remain clogged with plastic. Calling another levy “environmental” is no substitute for competent public services, and people are entitled to demand accountability for how their money is used. But government cannot tidy up a society that refuses to respect shared spaces: businesses and citizens have duties too. Order and cleanliness depend on both responsible leadership and personal discipline—not another slogan or tax.
